judgment.rationale:
Evidence from two sources reveals a mixed picture against CM-3.v3:

**Satisfied elements:**
- The initial deployment (CreateEndpoint at 2025-12-01T11:00:00Z) followed the model registry approval (2025-12-01T09:00:00Z). The approved model package (churn-predictor/v1, ARN: arn:aws:sagemaker:us-east-1:123456789012:model-package/churn-predictor/1) was registered and approved before the endpoint went live, satisfying the requirement that approved changes precede implementation (CM-3.d) for the initial release.
- A model registry entry exists, demonstrating some level of change documentation and approval workflow (CM-3.b, CM-3.c).

**Not-satisfied elements:**
- The UpdateEndpoint event on 2026-03-15T14:22:00Z (config: churn-predictor-v1-hotfix, performed by data-scientist-jdoe) has **no corresponding model registry entry**. This means the hotfix configuration change was implemented without a documented approval in the registry — violating CM-3.b (review/approve proposed changes), CM-3.c (document change decisions), and CM-3.d (implement only approved changes).
- The hotfix was applied directly by an individual IAM user (data-scientist-jdoe) without evidence of a change control board review or oversight body (CM-3.g).
- There is no evidence of a formal security/privacy impact analysis for either change (CM-3.b).
- Retention records for the hotfix change are absent from the registry (CM-3.e).

**Summary:** The initial deployment followed the approval gate, but the subsequent hotfix bypassed the change control process entirely — a material gap in configuration change control.
gaps: No model registry entry exists for the 2026-03-15 hotfix update (churn-predictor-v1-hotfix) — cannot confirm approval or impact analysis for this change.
No evidence of a formal security or privacy impact analysis for any change (CM-3.b requirement).
No evidence of a configuration change control board or equivalent oversight body (CM-3.g).
No evidence of a defined retention policy or audit log retention configuration for configuration change records (CM-3.e).
Human attestation needed to confirm whether an out-of-band approval process (e.g., ticket, email) existed for the hotfix that is simply not reflected in the registry.
